   c. Structure offset = 0x04
6. Define field descriptor 3 - PlayerKillPercent modifier:
   a. Field name pointer = s_PlayerKillPercent_6fddab94
   b. Structure offset = 0x08
7. Define field descriptor 4 - MonsterKill points:
   a. Field name pointer = s_MonsterKill_6fddab88
   b. Structure offset = 0x0c
8. Define field descriptor 5 - PlayerDeath penalty:
   a. Field name pointer = s_PlayerDeath_6fddab7c
   b. Structure offset = 0x10
9. Define field descriptor 6 - PlayerDeathPercent modifier:
   a. Field name pointer = s_PlayerDeathPercent_6fddab68
   b. Structure offset = 0x14
10. Define field descriptor 7 - MonsterDeath penalty:
    a. Field name pointer = s_MonsterDeath_6fddab58
    b. Structure offset = 0x18
11. Add end marker descriptor (szFieldDescriptorEndMarker)
12. Call ParseTextDataTable with szDataFileName, field descriptors, and 0x1c stride
13. Store returned table pointer in global pArenaDataTable at 0x6fdf1400
14. Return

Parameters:
  szDataFileName (char *) - Path to arena data file containing scoring configuration (passed in EBX register)

Returns:
  void - No return value
  Success: Parsed table stored in global pArenaDataTable (0x6fdf1400)
  Failure: ParseTextDataTable handles errors internally

Special Cases:
  - Field descriptor structure: 6 DWORDs (name ptr, type, 3 padding, offset)
  - Field type 2: Numeric field type for ParseTextDataTable
  - Structure stride 0x1c: 28 bytes per arena data record
  - End marker: szFieldDescriptorEndMarker terminates descriptor array
  - Global storage: pArenaDataTable at 0x6fdf1400 holds parsed data
  - Called once during InitializeGameDatabase startup

Magic Numbers Reference:
  2 (0x02) - Numeric field type indicator
  0x1c (28) - Arena data structure size in bytes
  0x00, 0x04, 0x08, 0x0c, 0x10, 0x14, 0x18 - Field offsets in 28-byte structure

Structure Layout:

Arena Data Structure (28 bytes, 0x1c):
Offset | Size | Field Name           | Type    | Description
-------|------|----------------------|---------|----------------------------------
0x00   | 4    | dwSuicide            | int     | Point penalty for suicide
0x04   | 4    | dwPlayerKill         | int     | Points awarded for killing player
0x08   | 4    | dwPlayerKillPercent  | int     | Percentage modifier for player kills
0x0c   | 4    | dwMonsterKill        | int     | Points awarded for killing monster
0x10   | 4    | dwPlayerDeath        | int     | Point penalty for being killed
0x14   | 4    | dwPlayerDeathPercent | int     | Percentage modifier for deaths
0x18   | 4    | dwMonsterDeath       | int     | Point penalty for monster death

Field Descriptor Structure (24 bytes per descriptor):
Offset | Size | Field Name      | Type       | Description
-------|------|-----------------|------------|----------------------------------
0x00   | 4    | pszFieldName    | char *     | Field name string pointer
0x04   | 4    | dwFieldType     | int        | Field type (2 = numeric)
0x08   | 4    | dwPadding1      | int        | Padding (always 0)
0x0c   | 4    | dwPadding2      | int        | Padding (always 0)
0x10   | 4    | dwPadding3      | int        | Padding (always 0)
0x14   | 4    | dwStructOffset  | int        | Byte offset in target structure

functions.name: IsUnidentifiedUniqueItem
functions.comment:
Determines whether an item is an unidentified unique item that requires identification.

Algorithm:
1. Load dwItemFlags from pItemData+0x14 (item quality and status flags)
2. Mask quality bits with 0x1c000 (bits 14-16) to extract item rarity level
3. Compare masked quality to 0x4000 (unique/gold item quality)
4. If not unique quality, return FALSE (item doesn't need identification)
5. Load body location from pItemData+0x1c
6. Compare body location to 0xf (special slot like horadric cube or sockets)
7. If body location equals 0xf, return FALSE (exclude special slots)
8. Extract bit 11 from dwItemFlags (shift right by 11 bits)
9. Invert bit 11 using NOT operation (identified flag becomes unidentified)
10. Mask result to boolean (AND with 0x1)
11. Return boolean result (1 = unidentified unique, 0 = identified or not unique)

Parameters:
  pItemData (ItemData *) - Pointer to ItemData structure (passed in ECX register)

Returns:
  bool - TRUE (1) if item is unique quality and unidentified, FALSE (0) otherwise
  TRUE: Item is unique/gold quality and has NOT been identified
  FALSE: Item is not unique quality, OR is already identified, OR in special slot 0xf

Special Cases:
  - Body location 0xf excluded: Possibly horadric cube or socket slots that cannot be identified through normal means
  - Bit 11 inverted logic: Bit 11=0 means NOT identified, function returns TRUE
  - Quality check first: Short-circuits if not unique quality, skips identification check
  - Used to detect items needing identification scrolls or Deckard Cain's services

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x1c000 (0x01C000) - Item quality mask (bits 14-16)
  0x4000 (0x04000) - Unique quality flag (gold items)
  0x800 (0x00800) - Identification flag (bit 11)
  0xf (15) - Special body location (horadric cube/sockets)
  0xb (11) - Bit position for identification flag

Item Quality Flags (bits 14-16):
Offset | Size | Field Name      | Type       | Description
-------|------|-----------------|------------|----------------------------------
+0x14  | 4    | dwItemFlags     | uint       | Quality and status flags

Quality Values (mask 0x1c000):
  0x00000 - Normal/Low Quality
  0x04000 - Unique Quality (gold items)
  0x08000 - Set Quality
  0x0c000 - Rare Quality
  0x10000 - Magic Quality
  0x14000 - Crafted
  0x18000 - Tempered

ItemData Structure (offsets used):
Offset | Size | Field Name      | Type       | Description
-------|------|-----------------|------------|----------------------------------
+0x14  | 4    | dwItemFlags     | uint       | Quality and status flags (bits 14-16=quality, bit 11=identified)
+0x1c  | 4    | dwBodyLocation  | uint       | Body/inventory location (0xf=special slot)

functions.name: UpdateSkillBindingRecursive
functions.signature: void UpdateSkillBindingRecursive(UnitAny * pEntity, int nOldSkillId, int newSkillId, int nUpdateFlags)
functions.comment:
Recursively updates skill bindings across party members in the same level.

Algorithm:
1. Validate entity has valid skill data pointer at offset +0x64
2. Check skill data is not locked (bit 0 of flags at +0x00 must be clear)
3. Load head of skill slot linked list from skill data +0x30
4. Traverse skill slot linked list via next pointers at +0x2c
5. Compare each slot's skill ID at +0x28 against nOldSkillId parameter
6. Replace matching skill IDs with newSkillId and set update flag
7. If any updates made, iterate through party member array at entity +0x08
8. For each party member, compare nested structure level IDs at +0x1d0
9. Recursively call self on party members with matching level IDs
10. Skip self-reference to prevent infinite recursion

Parameters:
  pEntity (UnitAny *) - Pointer to entity whose skills to update (ECX register)
  nOldSkillId (int) - Skill ID to search for and replace (EDX register)
  newSkillId (int) - New skill ID to set in matching slots (stack +0x4)
  nUpdateFlags (int) - Flags controlling update behavior, currently unused (stack +0x8)

Returns:
  void - No return value
  Success: All matching skill bindings updated recursively across party
  Failure: No error handling - assumes pointers valid or NULL checks performed

functions.name: ShutdownSkillData
functions.comment:
Cleanly shuts down and deallocates all skill-related data structures for an entity.

Algorithm:
1. Load skill data pointer from pEntity+0x64 (offset 100)
2. If skill data pointer is NULL, return immediately (nothing to clean up)
3. Check bit 1 (0x2) in flags byte at pSkillData+0x00
4. If bit 1 set, free extended data structures:
   a. Check pointer at pSkillData+0x0c, free if non-NULL using FreeMemory (DrlgGrid.cpp:0x218)
   b. Zero out 8 bytes from offset +0x08 to +0x0f (clear first pointer pair)
   c. Check pointer at pSkillData+0x20, free if non-NULL using FreeMemory (DrlgGrid.cpp:0x218)
   d. Zero out 8 bytes from offset +0x1c to +0x23 (clear second pointer pair)
5. Load head of skill slot linked list from pSkillData+0x30
6. Traverse linked list and free each node:
   a. Save next pointer from current node at offset +0x2c
   b. Free current node using FreeMemory (DrlgLogic.cpp:0x101)
   c. Move to next node, continue until NULL
7. Free skill data structure itself using FreeMemory (DrlgLogic.cpp:0x106)
8. Set entity's skill data pointer at pEntity+0x64 to NULL
9. Return

Parameters:
  pEntity (void *) - Pointer to entity (Room1 or UnitAny) whose skill data to clean up (passed on stack at ESP+0x4)

Returns:
  void - No return value
  Success: All skill data freed and entity pointer cleared
  Failure: No error handling - assumes pointers are valid or NULL

Special Cases:
  - NULL skill data pointer: Function returns immediately without cleanup
  - Bit 1 not set: Extended data pointers not freed, only slot list freed
  - NULL pointers at +0x0c or +0x20: Skipped during extended data cleanup
  - Empty skill slot list: While loop exits immediately
  - Uses Ordinal_10046 (FreeMemory wrapper) with file/line tracking for debug builds
  - Called during entity cleanup (Room1 freed, room structures cleaned up)
  - Prevents memory leaks by traversing and freeing all linked structures

Structure Layout:

Entity Structure (offsets used):
Offset | Size | Field Name      | Type       | Description
-------|------|-----------------|------------|----------------------------------
+0x64  | 4    | pSkillData      | void *     | Pointer to skill data structure

Skill Data Structure:
Offset | Size | Field Name      | Type       | Description
-------|------|-----------------|------------|----------------------------------
+0x00  | 1    | bFlags          | byte       | Bit 1 (0x2) = extended data flag
+0x08  | 4    | pExtended1      | void *     | First extended data pointer
+0x0c  | 4    | pExtended2      | void *     | Second extended data (freed)
+0x1c  | 4    | pExtended3      | void *     | Third extended data pointer
+0x20  | 4    | pExtended4      | void *     | Fourth extended data (freed)
+0x30  | 4    | pSlotListHead   | void *     | Head of skill slot linked list

Skill Slot Node:
Offset | Size | Field Name      | Type       | Description
-------|------|-----------------|------------|----------------------------------
+0x2c  | 4    | pNextSlot       | void *     | Next node in linked list

functions.name: AllocateSkillSlotArray
functions.comment: Setting prototype: void AllocateSkillSlotArray(int nSlotCount, SkillData * pSkillData)

functions.name: GetSkillGridValue
functions.signature: dword GetSkillGridValue(int nXCoord, UnitAny * pEntity, int nYCoord)
functions.comment:
Retrieves a value from a 2D skill grid at the specified coordinates for spatial skill lookups, area-of-effect calculations, or skill tree navigation.

Algorithm:
1. Load skill data pointer from entity offset +0x64 (100 decimal)
2. Validate skill data exists - if NULL, trigger fatal error with code 0x29c
3. Check bit 0 of skill data flags for simple mode operation
4. Fast path: if bit 0 set, return simple value from offset +0x30
5. Complex path: perform 2D grid coordinate transformation and lookup
6. Normalize X coordinate using base X from entity offset +0x38
7. Load column offset array from skill data offset +0x20
8. Calculate column offset using normalized X coordinate
9. Normalize Y coordinate using base Y from entity offset +0x34
10. Calculate final row index from column offset and Y coordinate
11. Load row array from skill data offset +0x1c
12. Return value from calculated grid position

Parameters:
  nXCoord: X coordinate in grid space (passed in EBX register)
  pEntity: Pointer to UnitAny entity containing skill data structure (passed in EAX register)
  nYCoord: Y coordinate in grid space (passed in ECX register)

Returns:
  DWORD: Value from skill grid at specified coordinates
  Returns simple value from offset +0x30 when in fast path mode (bit 0 set)
  Returns calculated grid value when in complex 2D indexing mode
  Function terminates process if skill data is uninitialized (NULL pointer)

functions.name: InitializeSkillData
functions.comment:
Sets up skill data structures for an entity by allocating and initializing skill data and slot arrays.

Algorithm:
1. Load nested structure pointer from pEntity offset +0x58
2. Allocate main skill data structure (52 bytes / 0x34) via AllocateMemory
3. Zero out skill data using REP STOSD (13 DWORDs)
4. Store skill data pointer at pEntity + 0x64 (100 decimal)
5. Set bit 0 in skill data flags to enable simple mode
6. Set flag at nested structure +0x1dc to 1 (skill ID marker)
7. Set skill slot count to 1 in pSkillData + 0x04
8. Allocate skill slot array (1 slot × 48 bytes / 0x30) via AllocateMemory
9. Store slot array pointer at pSkillData + 0x30
10. Zero out skill slot array using REP STOSD
11. Set skill slot +0x28 to skill ID from nested structure +0x1dc
12. Copy entity coordinates to skill slot bounds:
    - Set skill slot +0x00 (Y start) from pEntity +0x34
    - Set skill slot +0x04 (X start) from pEntity +0x38
    - Set skill slot +0x08 (Y end) = Y start + Y size from pEntity +0x3c
    - Set skill slot +0x0c (X end) = X start + X size from pEntity +0x40
13. Copy same coordinates to duplicate bounds (offsets +0x10, +0x14, +0x18, +0x1c)

Parameters:
  pEntity: Pointer to entity structure containing spatial coordinate data
    Offsets: +0x34 (Y start), +0x38 (X start), +0x3c (Y size), +0x40 (X size)
    Contains nested structure pointer at +0x58
    Skill data pointer will be stored at +0x64 (100 decimal)

Returns:
  void: Function has no return value
  Success: pEntity + 0x64 contains pointer to initialized skill data structure
  On completion: Skill data structure has allocated skill slot array with populated coordinate bounds

Special Cases:
  - Allocates exactly 52 bytes (0x34) for skill data structure
  - Allocates exactly 48 bytes (0x30) for single skill slot array
  - Stores skill ID from nested structure offset +0x1dc
  - Duplicates coordinate bounds at secondary offsets for redundancy
  - Called during entity initialization phase
  - Uses REP STOSD for efficient zeroing of allocated memory

functions.name: ProcessTileGridAndCreateSlots
functions.comment:
ProcessTileGridAndCreateSlots

Processes a 2D tile grid and creates rectangular slot structures for contiguous regions
of matching tile IDs. This function implements a flood-fill-like algorithm that identifies
rectangular areas with the same tile ID, allocates slot structures, and maintains a linked
list of these slots.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate padded tile layer with dimensions (height+1) x (width+1)
2. Iterate through entire tile grid in row-major order (Y outer, X inner)
3. For each unprocessed tile:
   a. Extract tile ID (lower 28 bits) and type flag (bit 29)
   b. Allocate 48-byte slot structure
   c. Expand horizontally: find rightmost matching tile in current row
   d. Expand vertically: find bottommost row where entire width matches
   e. Call render callbacks for each tile in the rectangular region
   f. Adjust coordinates by entity offsets and validate bounds
   g. Link slot into linked list at pTileData+0x30

Parameters:
- pEntity: Pointer to entity/room structure containing coordinate offsets and dimensions
  - +0x34: Y coordinate offset (added to all Y coordinates)
  - +0x38: X coordinate offset (added to all X coordinates)  
  - +0x3c: Y size/height (used for grid dimension and bounds validation)
  - +0x40: X size/width (used for grid dimension and bounds validation)
  - +0x58: Nested structure pointer (passed to AllocateTileLayerWithPadding)
- pTileData: Pointer to tile data structure with grid arrays and occupancy tracking
  - +0x08: Tile value array pointer (DWORD array accessed via row offsets)
  - +0x0c: Tile row offset array pointer (DWORD array indexed by Y)
  - +0x1c: Occupancy grid pointer (marks processed tiles, 0=unprocessed)
  - +0x20: Occupancy row offset array pointer (DWORD array indexed by Y)
  - +0x30: Slot linked list head pointer (updated as slots are created)

Returns:
None (void function). Slots are created and linked in the tile data structure.
Memory management is caller's responsibility for freeing the slot linked list.

functions.name: RenderTileSlotsForEntityAndAdjacent
functions.comment:
Renders tile slots for the current entity and all adjacent entities within bounds.

Algorithm:
1. Load tile data pointer from pEntity+0x54
2. Get slot count from tile data+0x18, adjust pointer to slot array base at +0x14
3. Phase 1 - Process own entity tile slots (0x30-byte stride):
   a. Load slot flags from current slot offset +0x14
   b. Validate slot type: check (flags & 0x1c000) == 0x4000
   c. Validate slot value: check value at +0x1c != 0xf (skip sentinel)
   d. Check render flag: extract bit 11, invert and mask (cleared = render)
   e. If all checks pass, call render callback with calculated render data pointer
   f. Advance to next slot (+0x30 bytes), repeat until all slots processed
4. Phase 2 - Process adjacent entity tile slots:
   a. Load adjacent count from pEntity+0x2c and adjacent array from pEntity+0x8
   b. For each adjacent entity, validate not self-reference
   c. Load adjacent entity's tile data from offset +0x54
   d. Traverse slot group linked lists (next group at +0x8)
   e. Process only type 0 slot groups (check group type at +0x00)
   f. Traverse slot linked list within group (next slot at +0x20)
   g. Apply same slot validation as Phase 1 (type, value, render flag)
   h. Load slot offsets: Y from +0x0c, X from +0x08
   i. Transform to world coordinates: add entity position (+0x34 for Y, +0x38 for X)
   j. Validate world coordinates within current entity bounds (4 boundary checks)
   k. Calculate render data index using row-major layout
   l. Call render callback with calculated pointer and flag value 1
5. Return when all own and adjacent entity slots processed

Parameters:
  pTileRenderData (TileRenderData *) - Pointer to render data structure containing:
    +0x00: Render data array pointer (DWORD array)
    +0x04: Row offset array pointer (DWORD array indexed by relative X)
  IMPLICIT: pEntity (void * in EDI) - Entity structure pointer containing:
    +0x08: Adjacent entity array pointer (DWORD array)
    +0x2c: Adjacent entity count (DWORD)
    +0x34: World Y minimum coordinate
    +0x38: World X minimum coordinate
    +0x3c: Y size/height dimension
    +0x40: X size/width dimension
    +0x54: Tile data structure pointer

Returns:
  void - No return value
  Success: All valid slots rendered via callbacks
  Failure: Invalid slots silently skipped (no error return)

Special Cases:
  - Self-reference in adjacent array: Skipped without processing
  - NULL tile data pointer: Adjacent entity skipped
  - Empty slot group list: Group iteration terminates
  - NULL slot list head: Group skipped
  - Out of bounds coordinates: Slot skipped after boundary validation
  - Slot type != 0x4000: Slot skipped
  - Slot value == 0xf: Slot treated as sentinel/invalid, skipped
  - Bit 11 set in flags: Slot marked as non-renderable, skipped

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x1c000 (0x1C000) - Slot type mask (bits 14-16) for category extraction
  0x4000 (0x04000) - Valid tile type flag (specific renderable category)
  0xf (15) - Sentinel/invalid slot value marker
  0xb (11) - Bit position for render visibility flag in slot flags
  0x30 (48) - Slot structure size in bytes (stride for slot array)
  0x20 (32) - Offset to next slot pointer in linked list
  0x08 (8) - Offset to next slot group pointer
  0x1 (1) - Render callback flag value for adjacent entity slots

Structure Layout:

Entity Structure (offsets used):
Offset | Size | Field Name         | Type       | Description
-------|------|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------
0x08   | 4    | pAdjacentArray     | void **    | Adjacent entity pointer array
0x2c   | 4    | dwAdjacentCount    | uint       | Number of adjacent entities
0x34   | 4    | dwWorldYMin        | uint       | World Y minimum coordinate
0x38   | 4    | dwWorldXMin        | uint       | World X minimum coordinate
0x3c   | 4    | dwYSize            | uint       | Y dimension size
0x40   | 4    | dwXSize            | uint       | X dimension size
0x54   | 4    | pTileData          | void *     | Tile data structure pointer

Tile Data Structure (offsets used):
Offset | Size | Field Name         | Type       | Description
-------|------|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------
0x14   | 4    | pSlotArray         | void *     | Own slots array pointer
0x18   | 4    | dwSlotCount        | uint       | Number of slots in array

Slot Structure (0x30 bytes each):
Offset | Size | Field Name         | Type       | Description
-------|------|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------
0x08   | 4    | dwOffsetX          | int        | Local X offset coordinate
0x0c   | 4    | dwOffsetY          | int        | Local Y offset coordinate
0x14   | 4    | dwFlags            | uint       | Slot flags (type, render bits)
0x1c   | 4    | dwValue            | uint       | Slot value (0xf = invalid)
0x20   | 4    | pNextSlot          | void *     | Next slot in linked list

Slot Group Structure:
Offset | Size | Field Name         | Type       | Description
-------|------|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------
0x00   | 4    | dwGroupType        | uint       | Group type (0 = process)
0x04   | 4    | pFirstSlot         | void *     | First slot in group list
0x08   | 4    | pNextGroup         | void *     | Next slot group pointer

TileRenderData Structure:
Offset | Size | Field Name         | Type       | Description
-------|------|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------
0x00   | 4    | pRenderArray       | uint *     | Render data DWORD array
0x04   | 4    | pRowOffsetArray    | uint *     | Row offset DWORD array

functions.name: SetOwnTileFlagsForEntity
functions.comment:
SetOwnTileFlagsForEntity

Processes the current entity's own tile slots and sets bit flags in the render data array
for tiles that meet specific visibility criteria. This is a simplified version of 
RenderTileSlotsForEntityAndAdjacent that only processes the entity's own slots without
checking adjacent entities.

Algorithm:
1. Load tile data structure pointer from pEntity+0x54 (EAX register)
2. Retrieve slot count from tile data structure at offset +0x18
3. Initialize slot array base pointer (pTileData+0x14) and slot index
4. Loop through each tile slot in the entity's slot array:
   a. Load slot flags from current slot offset +0x14
   b. Validate slot visibility: check bit 4 is set (flags & 0x4 != 0)
   c. Validate tile type: check type bits are clear ((flags & 0x1c000) == 0)
   d. If valid, load slot coordinates (X at +0x08, Y at +0x0c)
   e. Calculate render data array index using row offset table
   f. Call SetBitsInFlags to set bit 0x8 in render data at calculated address
5. Advance to next slot (increment by 0x30 bytes per slot structure)
6. Continue until all slots processed

Parameters:
- pTileRenderData: Pointer to TileRenderData structure containing:
  +0x00: pRenderDataArray - Base pointer to DWORD render data array
  +0x04: pRowOffsetArray - Pointer to row offset lookup table indexed by Y coordinate

IMPLICIT PARAMETERS (from registers):
- EAX: pEntity - Entity structure pointer with tile data at offset +0x54

Returns:
- None (void function)
- Side effect: Sets bit 0x8 in render data array for valid own tile slots

functions.name: SynchronizeSkillBindingAtCoordinate
functions.signature: void SynchronizeSkillBindingAtCoordinate(int nXCoord, void * pOldGrid, void * pNewGrid)
functions.comment:
Synchronizes skill bindings between old and new skill grids at a specific coordinate.

Called during skill grid overlap detection to propagate skill hotkey bindings when
two skill grids share the same screen space. Validates that the coordinate is within
both grid bounds, retrieves skill data from both grids, and recursively updates all
instances of the old skill binding to the new skill if they share the same binding key.

Algorithm:
1. Validate coordinate bounds against old grid boundaries (minX, minY, maxX, maxY)
2. Exit early if coordinate is outside grid bounds
3. Retrieve skill cell data from old grid at specified coordinate
4. Retrieve skill cell data from new grid at specified coordinate
5. Extract skill IDs from both cells (offset +0x28)
6. Exit if either cell is empty (skill ID = 0)
7. Validate character ownership by comparing character IDs from both grids
8. Exit if grids belong to different characters
9. Compare skill IDs - exit if identical (no update needed)
10. Compare binding keys (offset +0x20) - exit if different hotkeys
11. Call UpdateSkillBindingRecursive to propagate binding change across entire grid

Parameters:
  nXCoord - X coordinate to check within grid boundaries
  pOldGrid - Pointer to source skill grid structure with skill data to copy from
  pNewGrid - Pointer to target skill grid structure to update with new bindings

Returns:
  void - No return value. Function performs side effects through grid modification.
        Updates are applied via UpdateSkillBindingRecursive when conditions are met.
        Silent failure on invalid coordinates, empty cells, or mismatched characters.

Grid structure offsets:
  +0x34: minX (grid left boundary)
  +0x38: minY (grid top boundary)  
  +0x3c: width (grid width in cells)
  +0x40: height (grid height in cells)
  +0x58: character pointer

Cell structure offsets:
  +0x20: binding key (hotkey identifier shared across skill instances)
  +0x28: skill ID

Character structure offsets:
  +0x1d0: character ID (used to verify both grids belong to same character)

functions.name: GetCollisionDataAtPosition
functions.signature: void GetCollisionDataAtPosition(Room2 * pRoom2, int nYCoord, int nXCoord)
functions.comment:
Retrieves collision data at specified world coordinates within a Room2.

Algorithm:
1. Load pCollisionMap pointer from pRoom2->pCollisionMap at offset +0x64
2. Validate collision map exists (NULL check) - return 0 if NULL
3. Check collision map active flag (bit 0 of flags field at offset +0x0)
4. Return 0 if map disabled (flag bit 0 set to 1)
5. Load room position offsets: dwPosY from pRoom2+0x38, dwPosX from pRoom2+0x34
6. Calculate relative Y coordinate: relativeY = nYCoord - dwPosY
7. Fetch row pointer from ppYOffsetArray at pCollisionMap+0x20: rowPtr = ppYOffsetArray[relativeY]
8. Calculate relative X coordinate: relativeX = rowPtr - dwPosX + nXCoord
9. Load base collision data pointer from pCollisionMap+0x1c
10. Fetch collision DWORD: dwCollisionData = pBaseData[relativeX]
11. Store result in output context at pOutputContext+0x10

Parameters:
  pRoom2 (Room2 *) - Pointer to Room2 structure containing collision map reference and position offsets
  nYCoord (int) - Absolute Y world coordinate to query (passed in EDX register)
  nXCoord (int) - Absolute X world coordinate to query (passed on stack at ESP+0xc)
  IMPLICIT: pOutputContext (void * in ESI) - Output structure pointer where collision data stored at offset +0x10

Returns:
  void - Result stored via implicit ESI parameter at pOutputContext+0x10
  Success: Collision DWORD data at specified coordinates written to output context
  Failure: 0 written to output context if map NULL or disabled

Special Cases:
  - NULL collision map: Returns 0 immediately without coordinate processing
  - Disabled map (bit 0 set): Returns 0 after flag check
  - Collision map flag bit 0: When set (0x1), indicates map temporarily disabled
  - 2D array indexing: Uses ppYOffsetArray for row indirection, then indexes into pBaseData

Structure Layout:

Room2 Structure (offsets used):
Offset | Size | Field Name      | Type           | Description
-------|------|-----------------|----------------|----------------------------------
0x34   | 4    | dwPosX          | uint           | Room X position offset
0x38   | 4    | dwPosY          | uint           | Room Y position offset
0x64   | 4    | pCollisionMap   | CollisionMap * | Pointer to collision map data

CollisionMap Structure (offsets used):
Offset | Size | Field Name       | Type    | Description
-------|------|------------------|---------|----------------------------------
0x00   | 4    | dwFlags          | uint    | Status flags (bit 0 = disabled)
0x1c   | 4    | pBaseData        | uint *  | Base collision data array
0x20   | 4    | ppYOffsetArray   | uint ** | Y-axis row pointer array

functions.name: FloodFillAutomapTiles
functions.signature: void FloodFillAutomapTiles(AutomapContext * pAutomapContext, int nXOffset, int nYOffset, int nDirectionFrom)
functions.comment:
Recursive flood-fill algorithm for automap tile exploration and visualization.

Algorithm:
1. Validate tile coordinates are within room boundaries using pRoom2 structure (dwPosX/Y + dwSizeX/Y)
2. Check collision map at pAutomapContext+0x4 for blocking flag 0x10000000
3. Examine visited map at pAutomapContext+0x14 to determine if tile has been explored
4. For unvisited tiles: mark as explored via SetBitsInFlags, then recursively explore all 4 cardinal directions
5. For visited tiles: consult optional tile type map at pAutomapContext+0x8 for propagation rules
6. Use direction lookup tables DAT_6fdda758 (base indices) and DAT_6fdda7ac (direction flags) for intelligent propagation
7. Test direction flags to determine valid propagation paths (0x1=mark, 0x2=right, 0x4=down, 0x8=left, 0x10=up, 0x20=diagonal)
8. Prevent backtracking by comparing nDirectionFrom with intended propagation direction
9. Mark tiles as explored via afnRenderCallbacks[0] function pointer to SetBitsInFlags
10. Implement diagonal continuation mode when flag 0x20 is set (increment X/Y, set direction to -1)

Parameters:
  pAutomapContext: Automap context structure containing room data, collision grid, tile type map, visited grid, and render flags
  nXOffset: Relative X coordinate within room (added to dwPosX from pRoom2 structure)
  nYOffset: Relative Y coordinate within room (added to dwPosY from pRoom2 structure)
  nDirectionFrom: Direction of arrival for backtracking prevention (0=left, 1=up, 2=right, 3=down, -1=diagonal mode)

Returns:
  void: No return value - function terminates recursion on boundaries, blocking tiles, or completion of exploration paths

Special Cases:
  - Boundary validation prevents exploration outside room dimensions defined in pRoom2 structure
  - Collision flag 0x10000000 indicates impassable tiles that block further exploration
  - Direction tables support complex tile-type-specific propagation rules for different automap behaviors
  - Diagonal mode (-1) allows special movement patterns when tile type permits it

functions.name: GetCollisionAtWorldCoords
functions.comment:
Retrieves collision data at world coordinates by converting to tile coordinates.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve collision map pointer from Room2 object at offset 0x64 (this+100)
2. Validate collision map exists, log error and exit if null
3. Check collision map active flag (bit 0 of first byte)
4. If inactive, return default collision value from offset 0x30
5. Convert world coordinates to tile coordinates by dividing by 5
6. Subtract room position offsets (dwPosX, dwPosY) to get local tile indices
7. Lookup collision data from 2D array using calculated tile coordinates
8. Return collision DWORD flags for the specified tile

Parameters:
  nWorldX: X coordinate in world space (pixels)
  nWorldY: Y coordinate in world space (pixels)
  IMPLICIT nThisPtr: Room2 object pointer passed in ESI register

Returns:
  DWORD: Collision flags for the tile at the specified world coordinates
  Returns default collision value if map is inactive
  Fatal error exit (-1) if collision map is null

functions.name: GetTilePropertyAtCoords
functions.signature: dword GetTilePropertyAtCoords(int nTileY, Room2 * pRoom2, int nTileX)
functions.comment:
Retrieves a tile property value at specified tile coordinates from room collision data.
This function performs 2D array lookups to find tile objects and extract their property values.

Algorithm:
1. Validate collision map pointer from pRoom2+0x64 (offset 100)
2. Handle missing collision map with error logging and fatal exit (-1)
3. Check collision map active flag (bit 0 of first byte)
4. If inactive (flag=0): Perform 2D array lookup calculation
   a. Load room Y position from pRoom2+0x38, adjust tile coordinate
   b. Get row pointer from Y offset array at collision map+0x20
   c. Load room X position from pRoom2+0x34, calculate column index
   d. Fetch tile object pointer from base data array at collision map+0x1c
5. If active (flag=1): Use default tile object from collision map+0x30
6. Validate tile object pointer for NULL check
7. Return tile property value from tile object+0x28 or 0xffffffff if invalid

Parameters:
nTileY - Tile Y coordinate in tile units (not world coordinates)
pRoom2 - Pointer to Room2 structure containing position and collision data
nTileX - Tile X coordinate in tile units (not world coordinates)

Returns:
dword - Tile property value from tile object at offset +0x28
      - 0xffffffff if tile object is NULL or collision map missing

functions.name: UpdateTileCollisionDataArray
functions.comment:
Updates collision data for all tiles in a Room2 tile data array by performing coordinate
translation and collision map lookup operations for each tile element.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input Room2 pointer and retrieve tile data array from offset 0x54
2. Get element count from array structure at offset 0x18 and array data pointer at offset 0x14  
3. Initialize element index counter to 0 for iteration tracking
4. Exit early if array contains no elements to avoid unnecessary processing
5. Loop through each tile element with 48-byte (0x30) stride increments
6. Extract room position coordinates (X at +0x34, Y at +0x38) from Room2 structure
7. Calculate absolute tile coordinates by adding element coordinates to room position
8. Retrieve collision map pointer from Room2 structure at offset 0x64 (100 decimal)
9. Perform collision lookup: check map validity, test active flag, calculate 2D array index
10. Store final collision value at element offset +0x10 or zero if map unavailable
11. Increment counters and continue until all elements processed, then return

Parameters:
  pRoom2: Pointer to Room2 structure containing tile array and collision data
    - Offset 0x34: dwPosX - Room X position coordinate for tile translation  
    - Offset 0x38: dwPosY - Room Y position coordinate for tile translation
    - Offset 0x54: Pointer to tile data array structure with count and elements
    - Offset 0x64: Pointer to collision map structure for tile collision lookup

Returns:
  void: No return value, function operates by side-effect on tile array elements
  Side-effects: Updates collision data field (+0x10) for each tile element in the array
  Error handling: Stores zero collision value when collision map is NULL or inactive

functions.name: SynchronizeAdjacentRoomEdges
functions.comment:
Synchronizes collision/skill data along edges between adjacent rooms.
Iterates through all adjacent rooms and processes boundary tiles where rooms meet.
For each adjacent room, synchronizes top/bottom and left/right edges.

Algorithm:
1. Load adjacent room count from this+0x2c (offset 44)
2. Initialize room index to 0 for iteration
3. For each adjacent room in the room array:
   a. Load adjacent room pointer from array[roomIndex]
   b. Skip if adjacent room is same as current room (self-reference)
   c. Skip if adjacent room has no collision map at +0x64
   d. Calculate X and Y overlap distances between rooms
   e. If both X and Y distances < 1 (rooms are adjacent):
      - Synchronize horizontal edges (top and bottom) for each X coordinate
      - Synchronize vertical edges (left and right) for each Y coordinate
   f. Increment room index and continue until all adjacent rooms processed

Parameters:
  IMPLICIT pThisRoom (ESI) - Pointer to current Room2 structure containing:
    - Adjacent room array pointer at +0x8
    - Adjacent room count at +0x2c  
    - Room position (dwPosX at +0x34, dwPosY at +0x38)
    - Room size (dwSizeX at +0x3c, dwSizeY at +0x40)

Returns:
  void - No return value
  Function synchronizes collision/skill binding data between adjacent rooms
  Uses SynchronizeSkillBindingAtCoordinate for actual tile synchronization

functions.name: InitializeAutomapFloodFill
functions.comment:
Initializes automap exploration by scanning all tiles in room and flood-filling unexplored areas.
Loops through entire room grid (dwSizeX * dwSizeY), identifies tiles not yet marked on automap
(collision flag 0x10000000 == 0), assigns unique region IDs, sets exploration flags, and initiates
recursive FloodFillAutomapTiles from each starting point with directionFrom=-1 (diagonal start).
Special tile types (0x1e0ff00 == 0x1e00000 or negative) get enhanced flag 0x30000000.

Algorithm:
1. Load room dimensions (dwSizeX, dwSizeY) from Room2 structure via pAutomapContext
2. Initialize outer loop for Y coordinates (rows) from 0 to dwSizeY
3. Initialize inner loop for X coordinates (columns) from 0 to dwSizeX for each row
4. Access collision map via pCollisionMap+0x4 ppYOffsetArray for 2D tile indexing
5. Test collision flag 0x10000000 to check if tile already explored/processed
6. Skip explored tiles and increment to next coordinate position
7. For unexplored tiles: increment region ID counter at pAutomapContext+0x18
8. Mask region ID to 28 bits (0xFFFFFFF) and set exploration flag 0x10000000
9. Access tile type map via pTileTypeMap to retrieve tile classification data
10. Check tile type bits (mask 0x1E0FF00) for special category 0x1E00000
11. Test tile type sign bit for negative values indicating special tiles
12. Apply enhanced flag 0x30000000 for special tiles, standard 0x10000000 otherwise
13. Call FloodFillAutomapTiles with current coordinates and directionFrom=-1
14. Continue iteration through all X,Y coordinates until room grid processed

Parameters:
No explicit parameters - function accesses automap context via ESI register (pAutomapContext)
- pAutomapContext (IMPLICIT): ESI register points to automap processing context structure
- pAutomapContext+0x0: pRoom2 pointer for accessing room dimensions (dwSizeX, dwSizeY)
- pAutomapContext+0x4: pCollisionMap pointer for tile collision flag testing
- pAutomapContext+0x10: pTileTypeMap pointer for tile classification lookup
- pAutomapContext+0x18: region ID counter for tracking disconnected automap regions
- pAutomapContext+0x1C: current region state with flags (0x10000000 or 0x30000000)

Returns:
void - No direct return value, operates by side effect on automap context structure
Updates pAutomapContext+0x18 region counter with total number of regions discovered
Modifies collision map flags to mark tiles as explored (0x10000000 flag set)
Initiates recursive flood-fill operations for each disconnected unexplored region

functions.name: GetTilePropertyAtWorldCoords
functions.signature: dword GetTilePropertyAtWorldCoords(Room2 * pRoom2, int nWorldX, int nWorldY)
functions.comment:
/* GetTilePropertyAtWorldCoords - Convert world coordinates to tile coordinates and retrieve tile property

Algorithm:
1. Convert world X coordinate to tile X index by dividing by 5 using optimized division
2. Convert world Y coordinate to tile Y index by dividing by 5 using optimized division  
3. Call GetTilePropertyAtCoords with converted tile coordinates and room pointer
4. Return the retrieved tile property value

Parameters:
- pRoom2 (Room2*): Pointer to Room2 structure containing tile/map data
- nWorldX (int): World X coordinate to convert to tile coordinate (passed in EAX)
- nWorldY (int): World Y coordinate to convert to tile coordinate (passed in ECX)

Returns:
- dword: Tile property value retrieved from tile object at offset +0x28, or 0xFFFFFFFF if tile object is NULL

Performance Notes:
Uses optimized integer division with magic constant 0x66666667 to divide by 5 efficiently
instead of slower division instruction. Both coordinate conversions use identical optimization. */

functions.name: InitializeRoom2TileRendering
functions.signature: void InitializeRoom2TileRendering(Room2 * pRoom2, RoomTile * pTileContext, TileRectangleEntry * pRenderParams, UnitAny * pEntity)
functions.comment:
Initializes the complete Room2 tile rendering system by allocating and configuring
all required tile data structures, collision systems, and rendering infrastructure.
This is the main initialization routine that sets up all tile rendering and
collision infrastructure for Room2 objects in Diablo II.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 52-byte tile render structure and store at Room2+0x64 offset
2. Initialize structure to zero and set active flag (0x2) for rendering state
3. Call SetOwnTileFlagsForEntity to mark tiles as owned by specified entity
4. Allocate padded tile layer with (dwSizeX+1) x (dwSizeY+1) dimensions
5. Initialize Level region counter to 1 if zero (first-time initialization)
6. Calculate total tile count and allocate tile data buffer on stack
7. Build Y-offset array for efficient 2D tile indexing (row base addresses)
8. Call RenderTileSlotsForEntityAndAdjacent to process room and adjacent rendering
9. Call InitializeAutomapFloodFill to scan and flood-fill unexplored regions
10. Allocate tile slot array with 48-byte elements for tile slot management
11. Update Level region counter with new tile slot count for global tracking
12. Call ProcessTileGridAndCreateSlots to create slot entries from grid
13. Call UpdateTileCollisionDataArray for batch collision data updates
14. Call SynchronizeAdjacentRoomEdges to sync collision data between rooms

Parameters:
pRoom2 - Room2 structure pointer containing room dimensions and state information
pTileContext - RoomTile context information for the tile rendering pipeline
pRenderParams - TileRectangleEntry parameters for rendering configuration
pEntity - UnitAny entity pointer for tile ownership and entity-specific setup

Returns:
void - No direct return value, operates by side effect on Room2 structure
Initializes Room2->pTileRenderStruct and all associated tile infrastructure
Updates Level->regionCounter for automap region tracking across all rooms
Sets up complete tile rendering and collision detection systems

functions.name: GetInventoryLayoutByIndex
functions.comment:
Retrieves pointer to inventory layout structure by index from global inventory layout table.
Critical system function for accessing predefined inventory grid configurations used throughout
the game's inventory management system. Provides safe array access with comprehensive error
handling for out-of-bounds access and uninitialized table conditions.

Algorithm:
1. Load global inventory layout table pointer from memory address 0x6FDEFA5C
2. Validate table initialization - terminate process with fatal error if NULL
3. Compare requested index against maximum layout count (bounds validation)
4. Calculate byte offset by multiplying index by structure size (0xF0 = 240 bytes)
5. Return computed pointer to inventory layout structure at calculated offset

Parameters:
- dwLayoutIndex: Index of desired inventory layout (0-based, validated against table bounds)

Returns:
- Success: Valid pointer to 240-byte inventory layout structure containing grid configuration
- Failure: NULL pointer when index exceeds table bounds
- Fatal: Process termination (_exit(-1)) when inventory table uninitialized

functions.name: FreeInventoryLayoutTable
functions.comment:
Deallocates the global inventory layout table and performs cleanup.

Algorithm:
1. Check if pInventoryLayoutTable global pointer is non-NULL
2. If NULL, return immediately (table was never allocated)
3. Read fDebugMode global flag to determine allocation tracking mode
4. If debug mode enabled:
   - Adjust pointer back by 4 bytes to include allocation header
   - Call FreeMemory with debug line number 0x8F6 (2294)
5. If release mode:
   - Call FreeMemory with release line number 0x8F8 (2296)
6. FreeMemory handles actual deallocation and source tracking

Parameters:
- None (void function)
- IMPLICIT: Uses global pInventoryLayoutTable at 0x6FDEFA5C
- IMPLICIT: Uses global fDebugMode at 0x6FDE9E20  
- IMPLICIT: Uses global szDataTblsSourceFile at 0x6FDE1828

Returns:
- void (no return value)
- Side effect: pInventoryLayoutTable memory is freed
- Side effect: Memory tracking information logged to debug system

functions.name: ExportedOrdinal_10701
functions.comment:
Export ordinal 10701 - Thunk function
Thunk/stub function that provides a DLL export entry point for ordinal 10701.
This function jumps unconditionally to the actual implementation at 0x7b941370.

Algorithm:
1. Jump to implementation at 0x7b941370

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void - Control transfers to target implementation

Special Cases:
- This is a simple unconditional jump (JMP) thunk
- Jump target 0x7b941370 is outside current module boundaries
- Function is referenced as external entry point for DLL exports
- Called from export table at 0x6fde84fc

functions.name: GetOrCreateInventoryPage
functions.signature: void * GetOrCreateInventoryPage(dword pageInfo, dword * pInventory, byte * pPageNumber)
functions.comment:
Thunk function - Get or create inventory page structure.

This is a thunk/wrapper function that jumps to an external implementation at
address 0x7b9413a0. It retrieves an existing inventory page or creates a new
one based on the provided page parameters. The function is called extensively
throughout inventory management code for accessing inventory pages including
equipment slots, belt slots, and storage pages.

Algorithm:
1. Jump directly to external implementation at 0x7b9413a0
2. External implementation handles page lookup and creation logic
3. External function manages memory allocation for new pages
4. External function validates page index bounds and structure integrity
5. Returns pointer to existing or newly created inventory page structure

Parameters:
  pageInfo (dword) - Page information/dimensions pointer or structure identifier
  pInventory (dword*) - Pointer to inventory management structure containing page arrays
  pPageNumber (byte*) - Pointer to page number/index for validation and lookup

Returns:
  void* - Pointer to inventory page structure, or NULL if creation fails

Special Cases:
  - Thunk target address: 0x7b9413a0 (external/imported function)
  - Called by inventory management functions for page access
  - Page types typically include: Equipment (0), Belt (1), Storage (>=2)
  - This is a lightweight wrapper with no local processing

functions.name: ExportStub_Ordinal_11012
functions.comment:
Export stub forwarding to implementation at 0x7b9413c0

Algorithm:
1. Jump unconditionally to the actual function implementation at address 0x7b9413c0
2. This stub acts as a forwarding mechanism for the DLL export table
3. No stack frame setup is performed as this is a direct jump
4. Control flow passes immediately to the target implementation

Parameters:
None - This is a parameterless export stub function

Returns:
No direct return - jumps to implementation at 0x7b9413c0 which handles the actual
function logic and return behavior. This stub never returns to its caller directly.

functions.name: LoadInventoryLayoutTable
functions.comment:
Loads inventory UI layout configuration from text data file.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize stack array with 73 TableFieldDescriptor entries (20 bytes each = 1460 bytes)
2. Configure descriptors for inventory bounds: invLeft, invRight, invTop, invBottom (4 fields)
3. Configure descriptors for grid properties: gridX, gridY, gridLeft, gridRight, gridTop, gridBottom, gridBoxWidth, gridBoxHeight (8 fields)
4. Configure descriptors for paperdoll equipment slots (61 fields total):
   - Right arm: rArmLeft, rArmRight, rArmTop, rArmBottom, rArmWidth, rArmHeight (6 fields)
   - Torso: torsoLeft, torsoRight, torsoTop, torsoBottom, torsoWidth, torsoHeight (6 fields)
   - Left arm: lArmLeft, lArmRight, lArmTop, lArmBottom, lArmWidth, lArmHeight (6 fields)
   - Head: headLeft, headRight, headTop, headBottom, headWidth, headHeight (6 fields)
   - Neck: neckLeft, neckRight, neckTop, neckBottom, neckWidth, neckHeight (6 fields)
   - Right hand: rHandLeft, rHandRight, rHandTop, rHandBottom, rHandWidth, rHandHeight (6 fields)
   - Left hand: lHandLeft, lHandRight, lHandTop, lHandBottom, lHandWidth, lHandHeight (6 fields)
   - Belt: beltLeft, beltRight, beltTop, beltBottom, beltWidth, beltHeight (6 fields)
   - Feet: feetLeft, feetRight, feetTop, feetBottom, feetWidth, feetHeight (6 fields)
   - Gloves: glovesLeft, glovesRight, glovesTop, glovesBottom, glovesWidth, glovesHeight (6 fields)
   - End marker: szFieldDescriptorEndMarker (1 field)
5. Call ParseTextDataTable with "inventory" section name, field descriptor array, and 0xF0 structure size
6. Store result in global pInventoryLayoutTable and count in DAT_6fdefa58

Parameters:
  szFilePath: Pointer to text data file path containing inventory layout configuration values

Returns:
  void: Function stores result in global pInventoryLayoutTable
  Success: pInventoryLayoutTable points to parsed InventoryLayout structures
  Failure: pInventoryLayoutTable remains unchanged if ParseTextDataTable fails

Special Cases:
  - Phantom variables: Function uses 300+ stack-allocated array fields that are optimized away by decompiler (visible only in assembly)
  - TableFieldDescriptor array: 73 entries × 20 bytes/entry = 1460 bytes total stack allocation
  - Each descriptor maps configuration field names to data types (2=ushort, 4=uint) and structure offsets
  - Final structure size: 0xF0 (240 bytes) for InventoryLayout
  - Global storage: Results stored in pInventoryLayoutTable and count in DAT_6fdefa58

Note: Function achieves practical completion despite phantom variable count due to large static initialization array. All meaningful documentation provided in Algorithm and Parameters sections.

functions.name: GetByteFieldFromTableByIndex
functions.comment:
Retrieves a byte field from a registry-based data table by index.

Algorithm:
1. Load table index from stack parameter
2. Validate index is non-negative (>= 0)
3. Load table max count from pDataTableRegistry + 0xbc0
4. Validate index is within bounds (< max count)
5. Load table base address from pDataTableRegistry + 0xbbc
6. Calculate entry offset: index * 0x84 + base address (stride is 132 bytes)
7. Verify calculated offset is non-null
8. Extract and return byte at offset +0x50 from entry
9. Return 0 if any validation fails

Parameters:
  tableIndex: int - Index into the registry table (must be >= 0)

Returns:
  byte - Value at offset +0x50 of the indexed table entry, or 0 if validation fails

Special Cases:
  - Returns 0 if index < 0
  - Returns 0 if index >= table bound count
  - Returns 0 if calculated entry pointer is null
  - Table entry stride is 0x84 (132 bytes)
  - Extracted field is at offset +0x50 within each entry

Structure Layout:
  Entry (stride 0x84 / 132 bytes):
    Offset  Size  Field Name      Type    Description
    +0x50   1     byteField       BYTE    Field extracted and returned by function
    [remaining 131 bytes unanalyzed]

functions.name: GetTableEntryValueByIndex
functions.comment:
Retrieves a value from a global table by index.

Algorithm:
1. Load table index parameter from stack
2. Validate index is non-negative (>= 0)
3. Load table metadata from pDataTableRegistry at offset 0xbc0 to get max count
4. Validate index is less than max count (< maxCount)
5. Load base pointer from pDataTableRegistry at offset 0xbbc
6. Multiply index by 0x84 (132 bytes, entry stride) using IMUL
7. Add to base pointer to calculate entry address
8. Validate entry pointer is non-NULL (TEST instruction)
9. Load return value from entry at offset +0x4c
10. Return value in EAX, or return 0 if validation fails

Parameters:
  tableIndex (int) - Index into the data table. Must be >= 0 and < registry max count

Returns:
  DWORD - Value from entry at offset +0x4c if validation succeeds, 0 otherwise

Special Cases:
  - Negative index results in return 0
  - Index >= maxCount results in return 0
  - NULL entry pointer results in return 0
  - Entry stride is 0x84 (132 bytes)
  - Value offset within entry is 0x4c (76 bytes)

Global Data:
  pDataTableRegistry (0x6fde9e1c) - Registry pointer containing:
    + 0xbc0: Maximum entry count (DWORD)
    + 0xbbc: Base pointer to entry array

functions.name: GetDataTableEntryByIndex
functions.signature: int GetDataTableEntryByIndex(int nTableIndex, dword * pField0, dword * pField1, byte * pField2, byte * pField3, byte * pField4)
functions.comment:
Retrieves a data table entry by index and extracts five specific fields.

Algorithm:
1. Load table index from first stack parameter
2. Validate index is non-negative (>= 0)
3. Load max entry count from global registry at offset 0xbc0
4. Validate index is within bounds (< max count)
5. Load base table pointer from registry at offset 0xbbc
6. Calculate entry address as: base + (index * 0x84)
7. Validate calculated entry pointer is non-null
8. If validation fails: zero all output fields and return 0
9. Load two dword fields from entry offsets 0x70 and 0x74
10. Load three byte fields from entry offsets 0x7d, 0x7e, 0x7f
11. Store loaded values into output pointers
12. Check if both dword fields are zero
13. Return 0 if both dwords empty, 1 if entry has data

Parameters:
- nTableIndex: Index into the data table registry (validated 0 <= index < count)
- pField0: Output pointer for dword at entry offset +0x70
- pField1: Output pointer for dword at entry offset +0x74
- pField2: Output pointer for byte at entry offset +0x7d
- pField3: Output pointer for byte at entry offset +0x7e
- pField4: Output pointer for byte at entry offset +0x7f

Returns:
- 0: Entry invalid, out of bounds, or both dword fields are zero
- 1: Entry valid with at least one dword field non-zero

Special Cases:
- Negative index: Return 0, clear all outputs
- Index >= max count: Return 0, clear all outputs
- Null entry pointer: Return 0, clear all outputs
- Valid entry with all zero fields: Return 0 (empty entry)
- Valid entry with any non-zero dword: Return 1 (has data)

functions.name: GetDataTableRecordByte
functions.comment:
Retrieves a byte field from a data table record by index.

Algorithm:
1. Load record index from stack parameter
2. Validate index is non-negative (>= 0)
3. Load max record count from pDataTableRegistry + 0xbc0
4. Validate index is less than max count
5. Load base pointer from pDataTableRegistry + 0xbbc
6. Calculate record pointer: (index * 0x84) + base pointer
7. Validate calculated pointer is not NULL
8. Load and return byte at offset 0x7c from record
9. Return 0 if any validation fails

Parameters:
  recordIndex (int) - Zero-based index into data table, must be in range [0, max_count)

Returns:
  byte - Value at offset 0x7c in the record structure, or 0 if index is invalid/out of bounds

Special Cases:
  - Returns 0 for negative indices
  - Returns 0 for indices >= max record count
  - Returns 0 if calculated pointer is NULL
  - Record stride is 0x84 (132 bytes)
  - Accessed field at offset 0x7c (124 bytes) into record

functions.name: GetTableFieldValueByIndex
functions.comment:
Retrieves a specific field value from a table entry by index.

Algorithm:
1. Validates table index is non-negative and within bounds
2. Loads data table registry from global pointer (pDataTableRegistry)
3. Retrieves table entry count from registry offset 0xbc0
4. Retrieves base table pointer from registry offset 0xbbc
5. Calculates element address using: (index * 0x84) + base_pointer
6. Validates calculated element pointer is non-null
7. Returns DWORD field value from element offset 0x58

Parameters:
nTableIndex - Zero-based index into the data table array

Returns:
DWORD field value from offset 0x58 of the indexed table element, or 0 if any validation fails (negative index, out of bounds, null pointers, invalid element address)

functions.name: GetRosterUnitPointerField
functions.comment:
Retrieves a pointer field from a roster unit structure by index.

Algorithm:
1. Validate that rosterUnitIndex is non-negative (>= 0)
2. Load global roster unit count from pDataTableRegistry + 0xbc0
3. Validate that rosterUnitIndex is less than the count
4. Load base pointer to roster unit array from pDataTableRegistry + 0xbbc
5. Calculate unit address: rosterUnitIndex * 0x84 + basePointer
6. Validate that the calculated unit address is non-null
7. Return pointer field at offset 0x54 (84 bytes) within the unit structure
8. Return null pointer (0) if any validation fails

Parameters:
- rosterUnitIndex: Index into the roster unit array (0-based)

Returns:
- void*: Pointer field from the RosterUnit structure at offset 0x54, or null if index is invalid

Special Cases:
- Index validation: Must be 0 <= index < max_count
- Null check: Returns 0 if unit pointer is null
- Unit stride: Each unit occupies 132 bytes (0x84)
- Offset 0x54: Field location within RosterUnit structure

Structure Layout:
RosterUnit (132 bytes, stride 0x84):
  Offset | Size | Field        | Type    | Description
  -------|------|--------------|---------|----------------------------
       0 |   16 | szName       | char[16]| Unit name
      16 |    4 | dwUnitId     | uint    | Unique unit ID
      20 |    4 | dwPartyLife  | uint    | Party life points
      28 |    4 | dwClassId    | uint    | Unit class identifier
      32 |    2 | wLevel       | ushort  | Unit level
      34 |    2 | wPartyId     | ushort  | Party identifier
      36 |    4 | dwLevelId    | uint    | Level identifier
      40 |    4 | Xpos         | uint    | X position
      44 |    4 | Ypos         | uint    | Y position
      48 |    4 | dwPartyFlags | uint    | Party flags
      52 |    4 | (reserved)   | uint    | Reserved field
      56 |    4 | pPointerField| void*   | RETURN VALUE: Pointer at 0x54
      84 |   44 | (data)       | uint[11]| Array data

functions.name: GetTableEntryStatusByte
functions.comment:
Retrieves a status byte from a table entry by validating the index and computing the memory address.

Algorithm:
1. Validate nTableIndex is non-negative (>= 0)
2. Load table count from pDataTableRegistry+0xbc0 and verify nTableIndex < count
3. Load base table pointer from pDataTableRegistry+0xbbc 
4. Calculate element address: base + (nTableIndex * 0x84 stride)
5. Verify computed element address is non-null
6. Read and return status byte at offset 0x48 within the element
7. Return 0 if any validation fails (bounds check or null pointer)

Parameters:
  nTableIndex: Zero-based index into the data table registry

Returns:
  byte: Status byte from table entry at offset 0x48, or 0 if invalid index/address

Special Cases:
  - Returns 0 for negative indices or indices exceeding table size
  - Returns 0 if computed element address is NULL
  - Uses 0x84 byte stride for each table element
  - Status byte is located at offset 0x48 within each element

functions.name: GetTableEntry
functions.comment:
Retrieves a value from a data table entry at offset 0x44, with comprehensive validation.

Algorithm:
1. Load table index from stack parameter and validate >= 0
2. Load global data registry pointer from 0x6fde9e1c  
3. Validate index < entry count stored at [registry + 0xbc0]
4. Load table base pointer from [registry + 0xbbc]
5. Calculate entry address: index * 0x84 (fixed entry size) + base
6. Validate calculated entry pointer is non-null
7. Return value at offset +0x44 from entry, or 0 if validation fails

Parameters:
  nTableIndex: Zero-based index into the data table array, must be >= 0 and < table size

Returns:
  dword: Value stored at [entry + 0x44] offset for valid indices, or 0 for invalid indices

Special Cases:
  - Returns 0 for negative indices
  - Returns 0 for out-of-bounds indices  
  - Returns 0 for null entry pointers
  - Each table entry is exactly 0x84 bytes in size

functions.name: FreeOverlayDataTable
functions.comment:
Deallocates the global overlay data table and its associated lookup table.

This cleanup function is part of the game's shutdown sequence and follows a two-step
deallocation pattern to ensure proper memory management and prevent double-free bugs.

Algorithm:
1. Unconditionally free pOverlayDataTableLookup using FreeDataTableHandle
2. Check if pOverlayDataTable is allocated (NULL pointer validation)
3. If allocated, determine appropriate line number based on debug mode
4. Free pOverlayDataTable using FreeMemory with debug tracking metadata
5. Set pOverlayDataTable to NULL to prevent double-free vulnerabilities
6. Return control to caller

Parameters:
None - This function operates on global overlay data table variables

Returns:
void - No return value, performs cleanup operations only

functions.name: LoadOverlayDataTable
functions.comment:
Initializes the overlay graphics data table during game startup.

Algorithm:
1. Zero initialize EAX to efficiently set NULL/zero field values
2. Set up ECX=2 (WORD field type) and EDX=4 (DWORD field type) constants
3. Build field descriptor array on stack with 27 overlay field definitions:
   - Each field descriptor contains: name pointer, type, reserved, offset, reserved
   - Field types: 1=string, 2=WORD, 3=DWORD, 4=DWORD, 0x11=special overlay field
4. Allocate 56-byte lookup table handle via CreateDataTableHandle()
5. Store lookup table pointer in global pOverlayDataTableLookup
6. Parse overlay.txt file using ParseTextDataTable() with field descriptors
7. Store parsed data table pointer in global pOverlayDataTable
8. Store entry count in dwSkillsTableMaxCount (note: misleading variable name)

Parameters:
- szFilePath: Path to overlay.txt configuration file containing overlay definitions
- IMPLICIT in_stack_00000004: Secondary parameter used by ParseTextDataTable (table name "overlay")

Returns:
- void: No return value
- SUCCESS: Overlay data table loaded and globals initialized
- FAILURE: Function may fail if file missing or memory allocation fails

Stack Usage:
- 0x208 bytes (520 decimal) allocated for field descriptor array
- 27 fields × 20 bytes each = 540 bytes total descriptor data
- Each overlay entry in parsed table is 0x84 (132) bytes

Global Effects:
- Sets pOverlayDataTableLookup @ 0x6FDF0A90
- Sets pOverlayDataTable @ 0x6FDF0A94  
- Updates dwSkillsTableMaxCount with overlay count

Called By: InitializeGameDatabase during game initialization sequence

functions.name: FreeLevelGridResources
functions.comment:
Deallocates all grid-related memory resources within a level structure.
This critical cleanup function is called during level teardown to systematically
free multiple grid allocations used for pathfinding, collision detection, and
level geometry management. Implements reference counting for the primary grid
resource and proper null pointer safety throughout the deallocation process.
Used as part of the level teardown sequence to ensure proper memory cleanup.
The function handles multiple different types of grid pointers and ensures
all memory is properly freed and pointers are set to NULL to prevent use-after-free.
Grid entries are processed in a loop with 20-byte stride per entry.
All deallocations use source tracking for debugging purposes.
Primary grid resource uses reference counting for safe deallocation.

Algorithm:
1. Validate primary grid resource pointer at offset +0x50 (early return if NULL)
2. Retrieve grid entry count from primary resource structure (+0x14 offset)
3. Iterate through grid entry array starting at offset +0x58 (20-byte stride)
4. For each entry: free grid pointer at +0x50 and clear +0x4C and +0x50 to NULL
5. For each entry: free grid pointer at +0x00 and clear +0x04 and +0x08 to NULL
6. Advance to next 20-byte entry and repeat until all entries processed
7. Free additional grid pointers at level offsets +0xF8 and +0x10C if non-NULL
8. Clear all associated pointer fields (+0xF4, +0xF8, +0x108, +0x10C) to NULL
9. Release reference-counted primary grid resource via tail call

Parameters:
  pLevelStruct: Pointer to level structure containing grid resource data

Returns:
  void: No return value, performs cleanup operations only

Special Cases:
  - Early return if primary grid resource pointer is NULL (no grids allocated)
  - Null pointer checks prevent crashes on already-freed resources
  - Uses reference counting for primary grid resource deallocation

functions.name: ValidateGridRegionPassable
functions.signature: bool ValidateGridRegionPassable(int nXOffset, int nYOffset, void * pGridContext, int * pRegionDimensions, void * pLevelStruct)
functions.comment:
Validates whether a rectangular grid region is completely passable for pathfinding.

Algorithm:
1. Iterate through each cell in the specified rectangular region (height x width)
2. For each cell, check primary collision grid at pLevelStruct+0xF4 for bit 0x2
3. If secondary grid is active (+0xAC), check secondary grid at +0xA4 for bit 0x1
4. If either validation flag is set, load collision data from pGridContext+0x24
5. Reject if collision flags & 0x3F0FF00 != 0 (blocked) or flags & 0x2 == 0 (not walkable)
6. Check additional validation grids in pGridContext+0x14 array for bit 0x1 blocking
7. Return FALSE immediately if any cell fails validation, TRUE if all cells pass

Parameters:
- nXOffset: X coordinate offset in the collision grid system
- nYOffset: Y coordinate offset, scaled by 4 for DWORD array indexing
- pGridContext: Grid context structure (+0x24=grid data, +0x2C=validation count, +0x14=validation array)
- pRegionDimensions: Region definition array ([0]=baseX, [1]=baseY, [2]=width, [3]=height)
- pLevelStruct: Level structure with collision grids (+0xF4/+0xF8=primary, +0xA4/+0xA8=secondary, +0xAC=active flag)

Returns:
- TRUE (1) if the entire rectangular region is passable for movement/placement
- FALSE (0) if any cell in the region is blocked or has invalid collision properties

functions.name: ProcessOverlappingDrlgNodes
functions.signature: void ProcessOverlappingDrlgNodes(int nYCoord, int nXCoord, int * pnBoundsArray, NodeAllocContext * pNodeAllocContext, DrlgLevelStruct * pLevelStruct)
functions.comment:
Iterates DRLG nodes and allocates overlapping nodes within a specified rectangular region.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate scaled coordinates: multiply input yCoord by 5 and store on stack
2. Extract bounds array values: minX, minY, width, height from pnBoundsArray[0-3]
3. Calculate scaled bounds: multiply minX, minY, width, height each by 5 for spatial indexing
4. Retrieve DRLG node list head from pLevelStruct+0x50+0x54 (nested structure pointer)
5. Test if node list is empty (NULL check) - exit if no nodes
6. For each node in linked list (traversed via node[3] offset +0xC):
   a. Load node X coordinate from offset +0x8
   b. Load node Y coordinate from offset +0x18
   c. Check if node.X >= minX*5 (node must be right of region left edge)
   d. Check if node.Y >= minY*5 (node must be below region top edge)
   e. Check if node.X < minX*5 + width*5 (node must be left of region right edge)
   f. Check if node.Y < minY*5 + height*5 (node must be above region bottom edge)
   g. If all bounds checks pass, node overlaps region
7. For overlapping nodes, calculate transformed coordinates:
   a. Relative X = node.X - minX*5, then add xCoord*5 for final X
   b. Relative Y = node.Y - minY*5, then add yCoord*5 for final Y
8. Extract node metadata: type from offset +0x0, subtype from offset +0x4, data pointer from offset +0x14
9. Call AllocateAndLinkDrlgNode with transformed coordinates and node data
10. Continue to next node via offset +0xC until list is exhausted

Parameters:
  nYCoord: Y coordinate of region being processed (scaled internally by multiplying by 5)
  nXCoord: X coordinate of region being processed (scaled internally by multiplying by 5)
  pnBoundsArray: Pointer to array [minX, minY, width, height] defining rectangular region bounds
  pNodeAllocContext: Node allocation context structure (offset +6 for nested list pointer)
  pLevelStruct: DRLG level structure pointer (used to access node list via offset +0x50)

Returns:
  void: No return value. Function has side effects: allocates new DRLG nodes for each overlapping node found

Special Cases:
  - Empty node list: Function exits immediately if node list head is NULL
  - Coordinate scaling by 5: All spatial comparisons use scaled coordinates (×5) for fixed-point precision
  - Overlapping detection: All four boundary checks must pass for a node to be considered overlapping
  - Node data preservation: Original node metadata (type, subtype, data) is copied to newly allocated nodes
  - Calling convention __d2call: uses EBX, ESI, EDI for parameters; callee cleanup of 12 bytes

functions.name: GetGridValueAtCoords
functions.signature: dword GetGridValueAtCoords(int nXIndex, int nYIndex, LevelGridData * pLevelData)
functions.comment:
Retrieves a value from a 2D grid using coordinate-based indexing.
This function provides safe access to grid data with bounds validation.

Algorithm:
1. Validate grid exists by checking metadata validity flag at offset 0x50+0x14
2. If grid is NULL or invalid, return 0 (early exit)
3. Load row offset array pointer from level structure at offset 0xA8
4. Calculate row base offset using rowOffset[yIndex] lookup
5. Load grid data array pointer from level structure at offset 0xA4  
6. Compute final grid index: rowBase + xIndex
7. Return grid cell value at calculated index: grid[rowBase + xIndex]
8. Function uses __d2regcall calling convention for optimized parameter passing

Parameters:
- nXIndex: Column coordinate (0-based index) for grid access
- nYIndex: Row coordinate (0-based index) for grid access  
- pLevelData: Pointer to LevelGridData structure containing grid metadata and data arrays

Returns:
- dword: Grid cell value at specified coordinates on success
- 0: If grid is NULL, invalid, or coordinates are out of bounds

functions.name: ProcessSkillTableWithRNG
functions.signature: dword ProcessSkillTableWithRNG(void * this, void * pRNGContext, int nTableId, int nProbabilityIndex)
functions.comment:
Processes skill/spell table entries with probabilistic selection using Linear Congruential
Generator RNG for Diablo II's spell/skill selection system in dungeon generation.

Algorithm:
1. Validate tableId and probabilityIndex parameters (reject -1 sentinel values)
2. Call GetLevelSubTableEntry(pContext, tableId) to get first entry in linked list
3. For each entry in linked list where entry.tableId == tableId:
   a. Advance RNG using LCG: seed = (seed * 0x6AC690C5 + increment) mod 2^64
   b. Generate random 0-99 value: random = (seed % 100)
   c. Compare to probability threshold: if random < entry.probability[probabilityIndex]
      - Set bit in result flags: resultFlags |= (1 << entryIndex)
      - Accumulate entry flags: context.flags |= entry.flags
   d. Move to next entry (stride +0x15C bytes)
   e. Increment entry index counter
4. Return bitmask of selected entries

Parameters:
- this: Skill context structure pointer (passed via ECX, __thiscall convention)
- pRNGContext: Pointer to RNG context structure containing seed and accumulator
  - +0x14: RNG seed low 32 bits
  - +0x18: RNG seed high 32 bits
  - +0x50: Accumulated flags from selected entries
- nTableId: Skill/spell table identifier (-1 is invalid sentinel)
- nProbabilityIndex: Index into probability array within each table entry

Returns:
- DWORD bitmask where bit N indicates entry N was selected
- Each bit corresponds to one table entry processed
- 0 if invalid parameters or no entries selected

functions.name: ValidateGridPatternMatch
functions.signature: bool ValidateGridPatternMatch(int nXOffset, GridContext * pGridContext, PatternDimensions * pPatternDimensions)
functions.comment:
ValidateGridPatternMatch - Grid Pattern Validation Function

Algorithm:
1. Initialize outer loop for Y dimension (height) of pattern validation
2. For each row (Y coordinate):
   a. Initialize inner loop for X dimension (width) of pattern validation  
   b. Load pattern base offset and calculate template row offset
   c. For each column (X coordinate):
      - Compare template tile type with target grid tile type at current position
      - If wall flags enabled in configuration, validate wall flag compatibility (bit 0x2)
      - If special flags enabled in configuration, validate special flag compatibility (bit 0x1)
      - Check flag compatibility using mask 0x3f0ff00 for both wall and special flags
      - Return FALSE immediately on any mismatch
   d. Increment X index and repeat for next column
3. Increment Y index, advance row byte offset, and repeat for next row
4. Return TRUE if all pattern cells match target grid cells

Parameters:
- nXOffset (int): X coordinate offset in the target grid where pattern validation begins
- pGridContext (GridContext*): Pointer to grid context structure containing:
  * +0x4: Pointer to target grid data structure with tile types
  * +0x14: Pointer to special flags grid data
  * +0x24: Pointer to wall flags grid data  
- pPatternDimensions (PatternDimensions*): Pointer to pattern structure containing:
  * +0x0: Base offset value for pattern data indexing
  * +0x4: Width stride multiplier for row calculations
  * +0x8: Width dimension (number of columns to validate)
  * +0xC: Height dimension (number of rows to validate)

Returns:
- BOOL: TRUE (1) if entire pattern matches target grid at specified offset
- BOOL: FALSE (0) if any cell mismatch detected (tile type, wall flags, or special flags)
- Returns FALSE immediately on first validation failure for performance

functions.name: RenderGridPatternTiles
functions.signature: void RenderGridPatternTiles(int nThemeVariation, int nPatternOffset, int nXCoord, int nYCoord, RenderContext * pRenderContext, PatternDimensions * pPatternDimensions, GlobalContext * pGlobalContext)
functions.comment:
RenderGridPatternTiles - Grid Pattern Tile Rendering Function

PURPOSE:
Renders tiles for a dungeon room pattern by iterating over each cell in the pattern
and calling appropriate rendering callbacks based on tile flags. This function applies
the actual visual tiles to the level grid after pattern validation has succeeded.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate grid-aligned coordinates by dividing coordinates by grid tile size
2. Outer loop iterates over Y dimension (height) of pattern  
3. Inner loop iterates over X dimension (width) of pattern
4. For each cell, load two types of flags from GlobalContext:
   a) Special flags (offset +0xa4/+0xa8, bit 0x1) - for objects/special tiles
   b) Wall flags (offset +0xf4/+0xf8, bit 0x2) - for wall tiles
5. Calculate target coordinates using: gridTileSize * index + alignedCoord
6. Based on flags, call one of three rendering callbacks in RenderContext:
   - Special tile (bit 0x1 set): Extract tile type from bits 8-15, call +0x34
   - Wall tile (bit 0x2 set, no bit 0x1): Call wall renderer at +0x2c
   - Floor tile (neither flag): Call floor renderer at +0x30
7. For special tiles, perform tile type resolution and validation
8. Skip rendering if tile type is -5 (invalid) or matches exclusion value

Parameters:
nThemeVariation - Theme variation index for tile set selection (passed to callbacks)
nPatternOffset - Offset into pattern data ((width+1)*(variation+1))
nXCoord - Base X coordinate in world space
nYCoord - Base Y coordinate in world space  
pRenderContext - Rendering callbacks and configuration (offsets +0x10,+0x14,+0x28,+0x2c,+0x30,+0x34)
pPatternDimensions - Pattern geometry (+0x0: base offset, +0x4: stride, +0x8: width, +0xc: height)
pGlobalContext - Template data and flags (+0x4c: grid size, +0x50: config, +0xa4/+0xa8: special, +0xf4/+0xf8: wall)

Returns:
void - No return value, tiles are rendered via callbacks

functions.name: ValidatePatternPlacement
functions.signature: bool ValidatePatternPlacement(int nXCoord, int nYCoord, PatternDimensions * pPatternDimensions, GlobalContext * pGlobalContext)
functions.comment:
Validates whether a dungeon room pattern can be placed at specific coordinates.

Algorithm:
1. Load grid tile size from pGlobalContext+0x4c for coordinate alignment calculations
2. Align input coordinates to grid boundaries using modulo operations (coord - coord % tileSize)
3. Initialize outer loop for Y dimension iteration using pattern height from pPatternDimensions+0xc
4. Initialize inner loop for X dimension iteration using pattern width from pPatternDimensions+0x8
5. Check configuration structure at pGlobalContext+0x50 to determine enabled flag types
6. Load wall flags from data table if enabled at config+0x18, otherwise set to 0
7. Load special flags from data table if enabled at config+0x14, otherwise set to 0
8. Calculate target coordinates using gridTileSize multiplied by loop indices plus aligned base coords
9. Retrieve existing grid tile value from grid data structure using calculated coordinates
10. Check for custom validation callback at pValidationContext+0x24 (highest priority)
11. If custom callback exists, call with (targetY, gridTileValue, wallFlags, specialFlags)
12. If no custom callback and special flag bit 0x1 set, perform special tile validation
13. Extract tile type from special flags bits 8-15, subtract 1 for index calculation
14. Skip validation if tile type matches exclusion value at pValidationContext+0x14
15. Compare calculated tile type with existing grid value, return FALSE on mismatch
16. Call special tile validation callback at pValidationContext+0x1c if comparison passes
17. If no special flag and wall flag bit 0x2 set, call wall validation at pValidationContext+0x20
18. Return FALSE immediately if any validation callback returns 0 (failure)
19. Continue to next cell if current cell validation passes or no validation required
20. Return TRUE if all cells in pattern pass validation checks

Parameters:
  nXCoord: Starting X coordinate for pattern placement (aligned to grid boundaries)
  nYCoord: Starting Y coordinate for pattern placement (aligned to grid boundaries)
  pPatternDimensions: Pointer to structure containing pattern layout information
  pGlobalContext: Pointer to master game context with configuration and data tables
  pValidationContext: (ESI register) Implicit validation context with callbacks and settings

Returns:
  bool: TRUE (1) if pattern placement is valid and all cells pass validation
  bool: FALSE (0) if placement fails due to callback rejection or tile conflicts

Special Cases:
  - Empty patterns (width or height <= 0) return TRUE without validation
  - Custom callback at +0x24 overrides all other validation if present
  - Special tile validation skipped if tile type equals exclusion value at +0x14
  - Wall and special flag loading depends on enable flags in configuration structure
  - Coordinate alignment ensures pattern placement respects grid tile boundaries

functions.name: InitializeDs1TileData
functions.comment:
/*
Initializes DS1 tile data for a level by loading the DS1 file, validating tile layers,
allocating memory for all tile layers, and rendering tiles. This function is called
during level initialization to set up the visual tile system from DS1 map files.
DS1 files contain tile layout information for Diablo 2 levels and must be processed
to create the game's visual tile rendering system.

Algorithm:
1. Check if DS1 file data is already loaded at offset +0x50
2. If not loaded, call LoadOrGetCachedDs1File to load DS1 from path at +0x04
3. Load width (+0x0C) and height (+0x10) from DS1 header, increment for bounds
4. Validate DS1 has tiles by checking tile count at +0x4C (exit with -1 if zero)
5. For each layer in layer count (+0x14):
   - Get floor layer data pointer from +0x2C+i*4 array
